environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 6.0 service deployed on ECS Fargate in a private subnet. AWS Secrets Manager integration with automatic rotation configured via a Lambda rotator (template SecretsManagerRDSMySQLRotationSingleUser) on a 60-second rotation interval using RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays set to 0 with a custom schedule expression rate(1 minute). The task role has a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/DenyIMDSAndExternalNetworkBoundary) that denies ec2:DescribeInstances and restricts sts:AssumeRole. The VPC has no NAT gateway and no internet gateway attached to the private subnet; the only outbound path is through VPC endpoints for S3, Secrets Manager, RDS, and CloudWatch Logs (all with restrictive endpoint policies scoped to the account). The ECS task definition sets the awsvpc network mode with a security group that allows egress only to the VPC CIDR range (10.0.0.0/16) on ports 443 and 3306. DNS resolution for external domains returns NXDOMAIN due to Route 53 Resolver rules forwarding all non-internal queries to a blackhole DNS server (10.0.255.1). The connection string is injected at runtime from Secrets Manager and rotates every 60 seconds; any credential captured via XXE file read of environment variables or ECS task metadata would expire before an attacker could use it (rotation completes in <5 seconds, previous version is immediately staged for deletion via AWSPREVIOUS label removal).

config.internet_access: none - no NAT/IGW, VPC endpoints only
config.dns: Route 53 Resolver rules blackhole all external domains
config.secrets_rotation: AWS Secrets Manager, rate(1 minute), AWSPREVIOUS immediately removed
config.vpc_endpoints: s3, secretsmanager, rds, logs - account-scoped policies
config.imds: Fargate platform - no EC2 IMDS, task metadata v4 only
config.credential_ttl: 60 seconds max, rotated credentials invalidate previous
